{{short description|American mathematician (born 1943)}}
{{For|American bubblegum-blower|Susan Montgomery Williams}}
'''M. Susan Montgomery''' (born 2 April 1943 in Lansing, MI) is a distinguished American [[mathematician]] whose current research interests concern [[noncommutative algebra]]s:  in particular, [[Hopf algebras]], their structure and representations,  and their actions on other algebras. Her early research was on [[Group action (mathematics)|group action]]s on [[ring (mathematics)|rings]].

==Education==
Montgomery received her B.A. in 1965 from the [[University of Michigan]] and her Ph.D. in Mathematics from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1969 under the supervision of [[Israel Nathan Herstein|I. N. Herstein]].

==Career==
Upon receiving her Ph.D. from Chicago, Montgomery spent one year on the faculty at [[DePaul University]].  Montgomery joined the faculty of the [[University of Southern California]] (USC) in 1970 and was promoted to the rank of Professor in 1982. She was chair of the Department of Mathematics at USC 
from 1996 to 1999.<ref name=UscChair>{{cite web|title=USC Chair|url=http://www.usc.edu/uscnews/stories/4317.html|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref> Montgomery has spent sabbaticals at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], the [[University of Leeds]], the [[University of Wisconsin]], [[LMU Munich]], the [[University of New South Wales]], the [[Mittag-Leffler Institute]], and the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]].

Montgomery wrote about a hundred research articles and several books, of which ''Hopf algebras and their actions on rings'' is her most cited work. This book includes a discussion of Hopf-Galois theory, an area to which Montgomery has significantly contributed, and an introduction to quantum group theory.

==Honors==
Montgomery was awarded a [[Harry Frank Guggenheim Foundation|Guggenheim Foundation]]<ref name=GuggenheimFellows>{{cite web|title=Guggenheim Fellows Lists|url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/all?index=m&page=23|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130305044221/http://www.gf.org/fellows/all?index=m&page=23|archive-date=2013-03-05}}</ref> Fellowship in 1984 and a Raubenheimer Outstanding Faculty Award by USC in 1987.
 
She gave an [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS) Invited Address at the [[Joint Mathematics Meetings]] in 1984.  In 1995 she gave an Invited Address at the  Joint AMS-Israel Math Union Meeting in [[Jerusalem]].<ref name=AmsIntlJtMtg>{{cite web|title=International Joint Meeting |url=http://www.ams.org/meetings/international/1901_invited.html|accessdate=9 March 2013}}</ref> 
In 2009, she gave a plenary lecture at the summer meeting of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]].<ref name=CmsPlenay>{{cite web|title=Canadian Math Society Plenary Addresses 2009|url=https://cms.math.ca/Events/summer09/schedule_plenary_prize|publisher=Canadian Math Society|accessdate=11 March 2013}}</ref> She has also given numerous lectures at meetings and universities around the world.
 
Montgomery was the Principal Lecturer at the [[Conference Board of the Mathematical Sciences]] (CBMS) 1992 Conference on Hopf Algebras. Her CBMS monograph ''Hopf Algebras and their Actions on Rings''<ref name=HopfAlgebras>{{cite book |last1=Montgomery |first1=Susan |title=Hopf Algebras and Their Actions on Rings |date=1993 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |location=Providence, RI |isbn=978-0-8218-0738-5 |pages=238 |url=https://bookstore.ams.org/cbms-82|mr=1243637 |access-date=16 April 2021}} [https://books.google.com/books?id=1ePNAwAAQBAJ preview at books.google.com]</ref> is highly cited.  She has written one other book and has edited five collections of research articles.

She served as an editor for the ''[[Journal of Algebra]]'' for over 20 years. She was also an editor for the ''[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society|AMS Proceedings]]'', ''AMS Mathematical Surveys and Monographs'', and ''[[Advances in Mathematics]]'', and currently is on the editorial boards of ''Algebras and Representation Theory''<ref name=AlgRepThyEdBd>{{cite web|title=Algebras and Representation Theory Editorial Board|url=https://www.springer.com/mathematics/algebra/journal/10468?detailsPage=editorialBoard|publisher=Springer|accessdate=9 March 2013}}</ref> and of ''[[Algebra and Number Theory]]''.<ref name=AlgNoThyEdBd>{{cite web|title=Algebra and Number Theory Editorial Board|url=http://msp.org/ant/about/journal/editorial.html|publisher=Mathematical Sciences Publishers|accessdate=9 March 2013}}</ref>
 
Montgomery has been very active in the [[American Mathematical Society]], serving on the Board of Trustees from 1986–1996.<ref name=AmsBoardTrustees>{{cite web|title=AMS Board of Trustees|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/199604/from.pdf|publisher=American Mathematical Society|accessdate=20 March 2013}}</ref> She has also served on the Council, the Policy Committee on Publications,<ref name=AmsPublications>{{cite web|title=AMS Publications Committee Members|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/199910/officers.pdf|publisher=American Mathematical Society|accessdate=20 March 2013}}</ref> and on the Nominating Committee.<ref name=AmsNominatingComm>{{cite web|title=AMS Nominating Committee Members|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/200609/officers.pdf|publisher=American Mathematical Society|accessdate=20 March 2013}}</ref>

In 2013 she was elected to a 3-year term as a Vice-President of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name=AmsVicePresident>{{cite web|title=AMS Election Results|url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/elections/election-results}}</ref>  She was also a member of the [[United States National Research Council|National Research Council]]'s Board on Mathematical Sciences and Their Applications (BMSA), serving one year on the Executive Committee.

In 2012 she was selected a Fellow of the American Mathematical Society<ref name=AmsFellows>{{cite web|title=AMS Fellows List|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|accessdate=9 March 2013}}</ref><ref name=USC_AMS_Fellow>{{cite web|title = USC Announces AMS Fellows|date=November 2012 |url=http://dornsife.usc.edu/news/stories/1243/seven-up/|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref> and a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science|AAAS]].<ref name=AaasFellows>{{cite web|title=AAAS 2012 Fellows List|url=http://www.aaas.org/aboutaaas/fellows/2012.shtml|access-date=2013-03-19|archive-date=2013-03-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130323142745/http://www.aaas.org/aboutaaas/fellows/2012.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=UscAAASFellow>{{cite web|title=USC Announces AAAS Fellows|url=http://www.usc.edu/programs/wise/news/|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref>
